title: n8n vs Zapier Pricing: Which Costs Less? (2026)
summary: N8n vs Zapier differ primarily in their billing units: tasks versus workflows. See how this affects pricing and which approach suits your automation needs.
body_markdown:
## n8n vs Zapier: why the billing unit decides the price


### Direct answer and what each tool is


**n8n bills a whole workflow run as one execution, while Zapier bills every action step as a task.**


You can't compare their plan prices line for line, because they measure different things. Which one costs less depends on how many steps your workflows have and who maintains them, whether that's a developer comfortable with open-source tools like[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) or a non-technical teammate.


n8n is a workflow automation tool you can run on your own server or use as a hosted cloud service. It's built for people comfortable with branching logic, custom code and debugging their own flows.


Zapier is a hosted-only automation service built for non-developers, with a large app catalogue and a guided editor.


### Executions versus tasks, with a 10-step example


Take one workflow of ten connected steps (a trigger, then nine actions that look up a record, reformat it, write it somewhere and notify someone), which means a failure in any step breaks the downstream operations.


In n8n, that entire run is counted once, however many steps fire inside it. In Zapier, each action step that completes counts as a task, so the same run can consume up to ten.


Add a step and the gap widens. Fire the workflow more often and it doesn't.


### Shared n8n or Zapier accounts for agency clients


Stretch a workflow and n8n's unit looks better, while short two- or three-step workflows narrow the gap. For an agency, this is where **a shared account quietly cross-subsidises one client** .


When one client has a sprawling twelve-step onboarding flow and another a simple form-to-spreadsheet flow, the first can burn through the allowance the second barely touches, yet both get the same line on your invoice. Count steps per client before you quote a flat retainer.


### What the cheaper unit leaves out


**The cheaper unit isn't automatically the cheaper tool** , because Zapier's per-task unit does buy you something: you don't maintain servers or debug failed nodes yourself. That has a labour cost you should price in.


### How I verified n8n and Zapier billing definitions


I checked the billing definitions here against n8n's and Zapier's own pricing and documentation pages on 2026-10-16.


I've left out plan prices and allowance limits on purpose, because vendors change them and a stale number would mislead your quote. Pull current figures from those pages.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) meters the run, not the steps inside it: its pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, so a ten-step flow costs what the two-step workaround it replaced did, and you can set that against Zapier's per-task billing.
